raw_text:
# 12-Week Hypertrophy Programme: Vegan Female Recreational Lifter

## Client Snapshot & Assumptions

- **Client:** 26F, recreational lifter, strict vegan, full gym access
- **Goal:** Muscle gain
- **Training frequency:** 4 days/week (Phase 1), moving to 5 days/week (Phases 2–3)
- **Intensity method:** Reps in Reserve (RIR), i.e. how many reps she could still do at the end of a set
- **Before starting, please confirm:** bodyweight, training history (to set starting loads), injuries, schedule, and any specific muscle priorities. Many clients want glute/lower emphasis, but the plan below is balanced by default so you can adjust.

**A note on the 150g protein target:** Research supports 1.6–2.2 g/kg/day for hypertrophy. 150g is ideal for a client around 68–90 kg. If she's lighter, say 55–60 kg, 110–130g is fully sufficient and easier to sustain. The plan below hits 150g as requested, but scale it down if her bodyweight warrants.

---

## Phase Overview

| Phase | Weeks | Focus | Split | RIR |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1. Foundation | 1–4 | Technique, work capacity, baseline loads | Upper/Lower ×2 | 3 → 2 |
| 2. Accumulation | 5–8 | Volume progression (week 8 = deload) | Upper/Lower/Push/Pull/Legs | 2 → 1 |
| 3. Intensification | 9–12 | Heavier loading, peak volume (week 12 = deload + retest) | Upper/Lower/Push/Pull/Legs | 1 → 0–1 |

---

## Phase 1: Foundation (Weeks 1–4)

**Schedule:** Mon Upper A, Tue Lower A, Thu Upper B, Fri Lower B
**Rest:** 2–3 min for compounds, 60–90 s for accessories

### Upper A
| Exercise | Sets × Reps |
|---|---|
| Barbell Bench Press | 3 × 6–8 |
| Chest-Supported Row | 3 × 8–10 |
| Seated DB Shoulder Press | 3 × 8–10 |
| Lat Pulldown (neutral grip) | 3 × 10–12 |
| Cable Lateral Raise | 2 × 12–15 |
| EZ-Bar Curl | 2 × 10–12 |
| Cable Triceps Pushdown | 2 × 10–12 |

### Lower A
| Exercise | Sets × Reps |
|---|---|
| Back Squat | 3 × 6–8 |
| Romanian Deadlift | 3 × 8–10 |
| Walking Lunge (DB) | 2 × 10/leg |
| Leg Curl (seated or lying) | 3 × 10–12 |
| Standing Calf Raise | 3 × 10–12 |
| Cable Crunch | 2 × 12–15 |

### Upper B
| Exercise | Sets × Reps |
|---|---|
| Incline DB Press | 3 × 8–10 |
| Assisted Pull-Up / Pull-Up | 3 × 6–10 |
| Machine Chest Press | 2 × 10–12 |
| Single-Arm DB Row | 3 × 10–12 |
| Rear Delt Fly (cable or machine) | 2 × 12–15 |
| Incline DB Curl | 2 × 10–12 |
| Overhead Cable Triceps Extension | 2 × 10–12 |

### Lower B
| Exercise | Sets × Reps |
|---|---|
| Barbell Hip Thrust | 3 × 8–10 |
| Leg Press | 3 × 10–12 |
| Bulgarian Split Squat | 2 × 8–10/leg |
| Leg Extension | 2 × 12–15 |
| Back Extension (glute-biased) | 2 × 12–15 |
| Seated Calf Raise | 3 × 12–15 |
| Hanging Knee Raise | 2 × 10–15 |

### Week-by-Week Progression
- **Week 1:** Work at 3 RIR on all sets. Prioritise technique, and record every working weight. Use this week to identify weak points and movement restrictions.
- **Week 2:** Stay at 3 RIR. Add reps within each range. When she hits the top of the range on all sets, increase load 2.5–5%.
- **Week 3:** Move to 2 RIR. Add 1 set to the first compound of each session.
- **Week 4:** Hold 2 RIR at Week 3 volume. Use this as a checkpoint: review logs, energy, sleep, and bodyweight trend before Phase 2.

---

## Phase 2: Accumulation (Weeks 5–8)

**Schedule:** Mon Upper, Tue Lower, Wed rest, Thu Push, Fri Pull, Sat Legs, Sun rest

### Day 1: Upper (strength-biased)
| Exercise | Sets × Reps |
|---|---|
| Barbell Bench Press | 4 × 5–7 |
| Barbell Row (Pendlay or bent-over) | 4 × 6–8 |
| Standing Overhead Press | 3 × 6–8 |
| Weighted/Assisted Pull-Up | 3 × 6–8 |
| Face Pull | 2 × 15 |

### Day 2: Lower (strength-biased)
| Exercise | Sets × Reps |
|---|---|
| Back Squat | 4 × 5–7 |
| Conventional or Trap-Bar Deadlift | 3 × 5 |
| Barbell Hip Thrust | 3 × 8 |
| Lying Leg Curl | 3 × 8–10 |
| Standing Calf Raise | 3 × 8–10 |

### Day 3: Push (hypertrophy)
| Exercise | Sets × Reps |
|---|---|
| Incline DB Press | 4 × 8–10 |
| Machine Shoulder Press | 3 × 10–12 |
| Cable Fly (low-to-high) | 3 × 12–15 |
| Cable/DB Lateral Raise | 4 × 12–20 |
| Dips (assisted if needed) | 3 × 8–12 |
| Overhead Triceps Extension | 3 × 10–12 |

### Day 4: Pull (hypertrophy)
| Exercise | Sets × Reps |
|---|---|
| Lat Pulldown (wide) | 4 × 10–12 |
| Seated Cable Row | 3 × 10–12 |
| Single-Arm Lat Pullover (cable) | 3 × 12–15 |
| Reverse Pec Deck | 3 × 15–20 |
| Barbell or EZ Curl | 3 × 8–12 |
| Hammer Curl | 2 × 10–12 |

### Day 5: Legs (hypertrophy)
| Exercise | Sets × Reps |
|---|---|
| Hack Squat or Leg Press | 4 × 10–12 |
| Romanian Deadlift | 3 × 10–12 |
| Bulgarian Split Squat | 3 × 10/leg |
| Leg Extension | 3 × 15 |
| Seated Leg Curl | 3 × 12–15 |
| Cable Hip Abduction or Machine Abductor | 3 × 15–20 |
| Seated Calf Raise | 3 × 15 |
| Cable Crunch / Ab Wheel | 3 × 10–15 |

### Week-by-Week Progression
- **Week 5:** Work at 2 RIR. Re-establish loads for the new exercises.
- **Week 6:** Stay at 2 RIR. Add 1 set to one isolation exercise per muscle group, prioritising laterals, leg curls, and rows.
- **Week 7:** Move to 1 RIR on accessories and keep 2 RIR on heavy compounds. This is peak Phase 2 volume.
- **Week 8 (Deload):** Use the same exercises, cut sets by about 50%, reduce load by about 10%, and train at 3–4 RIR. Push sleep and calories here.

---

## Phase 3: Intensification (Weeks 9–12)

Phase 3 keeps the same 5-day split, with these changes:
- Compounds move to lower reps: Bench and Squat at **4 × 4–6**, Deadlift at **3 × 3–5**.
- Swap a few hypertrophy-day exercises for novelty: Incline DB Press becomes Incline Smith Press, Hack Squat becomes Pendulum/Belt Squat if available, and Lat Pulldown becomes Kneeling Single-Arm Pulldown.
- Add one intensity technique to the **last set of 1–2 isolation exercises** per session, such as a drop set, myo-reps, or lengthened partials. Avoid these on heavy compounds.

### Week-by-Week Progression
- **Week 9:** Work at 1–2 RIR. Begin heavier compound ranges.
- **Week 10:** Move to 1 RIR. Add 1 set to the main compound on each strength day.
- **Week 11:** Use 0–1 RIR on isolations and 1 RIR on compounds. This is peak training stress, so watch recovery closely.
- **Week 12 (Deload + Retest):** Mon–Wed are deload sessions at 50% volume. Thu or Fri, test a rep max (e.g. 5RM on Squat, Bench, Hip Thrust, plus max pull-ups) against Week 1–2 numbers. Take progress photos and measurements.

---

## Nutrition Plan: 150g Plant Protein/Day

### Calorie Target
Set calories at estimated maintenance plus 200–300 kcal for a lean gain. Aim for **0.25–0.5% bodyweight gain per week**. Weigh her 3–4 mornings per week and use the weekly average to adjust intake by ±150 kcal every 2 weeks as needed.

### Macronutrient Guide
- **Protein:** 150g (or 1.6–2.2 g/kg)
- **Fat:** 0.8–1 g/kg minimum, including nuts, seeds, avocado, and olive oil
- **Carbohydrate:** fill the remaining calories, since carbs fuel training volume

### Protein Quality
Plant proteins are complete when varied across the day. Soy, seitan plus legumes, and pea/rice blends cover all essential amino acids. Aim for **30–40g per meal** across 4 feedings. Plant proteins are slightly lower in leucine, so slightly larger servings help.

### Sample Day (~150–160g protein, ~2,200–2,400 kcal)

| Meal | Foods | Protein |
|---|---|---|
| **Breakfast** | 80g oats cooked in 300ml soy milk, with 30g pea/soy protein powder, 1 tbsp ground flax, and berries | ~45g |
| **Lunch** | 150g tempeh (marinated, pan-fried), 1 cup cooked quinoa, roasted vegetables, and tahini dressing | ~42g |
| **Snack** | 150g shelled edamame, or high-protein soy yoghurt with 20g pumpkin seeds | ~17–20g |
| **Dinner** | 200g extra-firm tofu stir-fry with vegetables, 80g dry red-lentil or edamame pasta, and a peanut sauce | ~50g |
| **Optional** | Soy milk shake or 2 slices wholegrain toast with peanut butter | +10–15g |

*Protein values vary by brand, especially tofu (8–17g/100g) and yoghurts, so have her check labels.*

### High-Protein Rotation List
- **Seitan:** ~25g per 100g
- **TVP:** ~50g per 100g dry; great in chilli or bolognese
- **Tempeh:** ~20g per 100g
- **Extra-firm tofu:** ~15g per 100g
- **Lentils/chickpeas/black beans:** ~15–18g per cooked cup
- **Edamame/lentil pastas:** ~20–25g per 80g dry
- **Pea, soy, or blended vegan protein powders:** ~20–25g per scoop
- **Soy milk:** ~7–8g per cup, far more than oat or almond milk

### Supplements for Vegan Clients
Recommend she discusses these with her GP or a dietitian, ideally with baseline bloods (ferritin, B12, vitamin D).
- **Vitamin B12:** essential for vegans
- **Vitamin D3:** use a lichen-derived (vegan) form, especially in winter
- **Algae-based omega-3 (EPA/DHA)**
- **Creatine monohydrate, 3–5 g/day:** typically synthetic and vegan-friendly. Vegans often have lower baseline muscle creatine and may respond especially well.
- **Iodine:** from iodised salt or a supplement
- **Iron, zinc, and calcium:** monitor these. Pair iron-rich foods with vitamin C. Choose calcium-set tofu and fortified milks.

### Digestive Tolerance
Fibre intake on this plan will be high. Ramp legumes up over 1–2 weeks, encourage plenty of water, and use powders, seitan, and tofu if bloating limits appetite.

---

## Recovery

- **Sleep:** 7–9 hours. This is the single biggest recovery lever.
- **Steps:** 7–10k daily. Keep cardio low-moderate, e.g. 2 × 20 min zone 2, so it doesn't eat into her surplus.
- **Menstrual cycle:** If she notices performance or energy dips, let her autoregulate using RIR rather than forcing loads. Many clients feel strongest in the follicular phase.
- **Monitor weekly:** sleep, soreness, energy, appetite, and bodyweight trend. If two or more decline for over a week, pull the deload forward.
- **Mobility:** 5–10 min of dynamic warm-up before sessions, focused on hips, T-spine, and ankles.

---

## Assessment Checkpoints

| Week | What to Check |
|---|---|
| 0 | Bodyweight, measurements (waist, hips, glutes, thigh, arm), photos, baseline loads |
| 4 | Bodyweight trend, technique review, adherence to the nutrition plan |
| 8 | Measurements, photos, calorie adjustment |
| 12 | Full retest: rep maxes, measurements, photos, and planning for the next block |

If you share her bodyweight and any muscle priorities, I can tighten the calorie and protein numbers and rebalance volume, e.g. adding a glute-focused bias or a 4-day version if her schedule is limited.
